newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end down as Telekom falters.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end down as Telekom falters.

text.p: A sharp fall of key blue chip telecommunications firm Telekom pulled the market down to a lower finish on Wednesday, analysts said.
At the close, the key Composite Index of large-capitalised stocks fell 6.87 points or 0.67 percent to 1,024.74.
Expectations that Telekom would post less-than-spectacular annual profits caused selling of the stock, which fell 35 cents to 9.95 ringgit on volume of 4.1 million shares traded.
"If Telekom results are 930 million (in net profits), it's more excuse to sell," said Victor Wan, senior analyst at South Johor Securities.

Telekom shares earlier dipped to a new 1997 low of 9.85 ringgit. Analysts said there was talk that Telekom would report net profit of 930 to 950 million ringgit for the half-year to June 30, 1997. It is expected to release results on Friday.
"It's slightly below expectations. The growth will be very slow, about 10 percent" compared with 22 percent last year, said Soon Teck Onn, telecommunications analyst at ING-Barings.

Other large-capitalised issues also fell back in the largely newsless session. Dealers said with investors focusing on negatives, unconfirmed talk that Malaysia will post a trade deficit in June did not help.
